headline: Aspinall whitewashes Sedláček 5-0: ‘I’ve never felt better’
standfirst: Nathan Aspinall finished the Grand Slam group stage unbeaten and says harder work away from the oche is behind his form.
body: Nathan Aspinall secured his place in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts by beating Karel Sedláček 5-0, finishing the group stage unbeaten. He plays Gabriel Clemens in the next round on Thursday.

Aspinall averaged around 102 against Sedláček, though he had thought his overall group average was higher. "I think I averaged 107 or 108 for the group," he said. He knew he needed only three legs to progress but said he did not want that to change his approach.

He noticed that Sedláček was scoring well but missing his doubles, and admitted to some nerves going into the third leg, the one that sealed qualification. Once through, he said he wanted to entertain the crowd and had hoped to hit a 170 finish or even a nine-darter, though neither chance came.

Aspinall said the improvement in his results is no accident. "This is the best I've felt since I've ever played darts," he told reporters, adding that he is looking after himself and has been working harder than at any time in the last five years. He also said he had spent part of the morning on the phone to people close to him to get his head right before the match.
He also had a message for those he feels do not give him enough credit for what he has achieved in the sport, and spoke of his desire to win major titles again.
Aspinall has climbed three places to eighth in the provisional Order of Merit after the group stage, and a deep run in Wolverhampton could lift him further.
